## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Niyāmakathā* (Kv 6.1) is a debate text in the *Kathāvatthu*, the fifth treatise of the Theravāda Abhidhamma Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. It constitutes the opening section of the sixth chapter (*vagga*) of the work [SuttaCentral]. In the Pali Text Society's English translation of the *Kathāvatthu* (*Points of Controversy*), the doctrinal term *niyāma* is rendered as "Assurance" [Dube 1980]. SuttaCentral records one modern translation in one language [SuttaCentral].

No historical parallels in other early Buddhist collections are identified by SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral]. Computational analysis by DharmaNexus identifies extensive Pali-internal text reuse, recording 333 matching passages across 21 other Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. These reuses primarily reflect the formulaic dialectical framing shared with other debates in the *Kathāvatthu*, most prominently the immediately following *Paṭiccasamuppādakathā* (Kv 6.2, sharing 40 matches and 4,099 characters, with its longest shared passage spanning §0.1–5.2 ↔ §0.1–2.2 at 0.89 similarity), the *Sāmaññaphalakathā* (Kv 19.3), the *Pattikathā* (Kv 19.4), the *Saccakathā* (Kv 6.3), the *Nirodhasamāpattikathā* (Kv 6.5), and the *Puggalakathā* (Kv 1.1) [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language matches, DharmaNexus automatically aligns passages of the text with Tibetan translations of Mahāyāna scriptures, including the *Aṣṭādaśasāhasrikā-prajñāpāramitā* (D0010-3) and the *Śatasāhasrikā-prajñāpāramitā* (D0008-12); these represent automatic phrase-level correspondences rather than curated doctrinal parallels [DharmaNexus].

In modern secondary literature, the *Niyāmakathā* is not discussed at length in the provided sources, being cited only in passing regarding the translation of *niyāma* as "Assurance" in *Points of Controversy* [Dube 1980].
